This is weakly supportive for a high prediction, but the transferability is limited because tacrolimus has very different physicochemical and structural features.

MOLECULE 2 | RECORD C24  
ANALYSIS: This record describes a predicted human oral bioavailability of 80% for a compound containing a cyclopentyl group and a heteroaromatic lactam/amide system, which are motifs also present in the query. Although the value is predicted rather than experimentally measured, it supports the idea that compounds in this general chemical space can have high oral bioavailability. Transferability is moderate and supportive.

MOLECULE 3 | RECORDS C32, C12, C13  
ANALYSIS: Brigatinib is an aminopyrimidine–aniline kinase inhibitor bearing a piperazine-containing solubilizing group, making it structurally and mechanistically relevant to the query. Its absolute oral bioavailability was 77% in the fed state, 57% in the fasted state, and approximately 46% in a radiolabeled healthy-volunteer study. All values are clearly above the 20% threshold. This is strong, transferable supportive evidence for a high prediction.

Although the exact scaffold differs, the presence of a nitrogen-rich heteroaromatic system and the high measured F value support the conclusion that such compounds are generally well absorbed orally. This is supportive evidence with moderate-to-good transferability.

MOLECULE 5 | RECORD C03  
ANALYSIS: Imatinib is an aminopyrimidine–piperazine kinase inhibitor with a mean absolute oral bioavailability of 98%. This is one of the most structurally relevant comparators because it shares the aminopyrimidine and piperazine-aniline motifs with the query. The very high F value strongly supports a high bioavailability prediction for the query.

ANALYSIS: Fasudil is a piperazine-containing heteroaromatic drug with an absolute oral bioavailability of 69% in humans. Although its mechanism and scaffold differ from the query, the high measured F value adds general supportive evidence that piperazine-containing oral drugs in this property range can achieve high bioavailability. Transferability is moderate.

ANALYSIS: Risdiplam is reported to have high oral bioavailability, with essentially complete absorption, negligible intestinal extraction, and low hepatic extraction. These records consistently support a high F prediction, although the exact structural overlap is not complete.

This record does not affirmatively establish low bioavailability; it is too uncertain and variable to serve as threshold-relevant evidence for a low prediction. The repeated high F values across independent studies provide strong supportive evidence for the query, despite scaffold differences.
